prompt: A 55-year-old male is admitted to the hospital with extensive skin lesions and is suspected to have Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). The patient has a history of prostate cancer and is currently undergoing chemotherapy. On examination, he exhibits a heart rate of 130 beats per minute. Initial evaluation reveals that approximately 15% of his body surface area is affected by epidermal detachment. Laboratory tests show a serum urea level of 12 mmol/L, a serum glucose level of 16 mmol/L, and a serum bicarbonate level of 18 mmol/L. The medical team wants to assess the severity of his condition using the SCORTEN score. What is this patient's SCORTEN score and what does it imply about his prognosis?

rubric_items.text: States the SCORTEN score is 7 (out of 7; exact integer match required).
States that a SCORTEN of 7 (≥5) predicts very high mortality, approximately 90%.
